sets.context:
Arnav, Bhavna, Cyrus, Divya, Esha and Farhan are six friends. Each uses a number from exactly one of two operators — Metro (Arnav, Cyrus, Esha) and Nova (Bhavna, Divya, Farhan). Last month they sent text messages to one another (all counts are multiples of 10). The grid shows messages sent by each friend (row) to each other (column), with the operator-wise outgoing totals (Out-Metro, Out-Nova) on the right and the operator-wise incoming totals (In-Metro, In-Nova) at the bottom. A cell showing 0 means no messages were sent in that direction; blank inner cells are unknown.
It is additionally known that Farhan sent 30 messages to Arnav. Additionally, each of Bhavna and Divya sent some messages to both Arnav and Esha.

questions.prompt: How many messages did Cyrus send to Divya?
explanations: Incorrect. The solved table arrives at option B, not option A.

Correct. Deduction: The operator-wise outgoing and incoming totals, together with the 0 (forbidden) cells, fix every inner cell except a 2×2 block. Cyrus's only Metro recipients are Arnav/Esha (both 0), so his Nova row 30/40/20 to Bhavna/Divya/Farhan is forced; Cyrus→Divya = 40. Column totals force Arnav's incoming = In-Metro 0 + In-Nova 60 = 60. The cells Bhavna→Arnav, Bhavna→Esha, Divya→Arnav, Divya→Esha form a degenerate loop: each is 10 or 20 (with Bhavna→Arnav and Divya→Esha equal, and the other pair equal) — two solutions, |S| = 2.

Q1: Cyrus→Divya = 40 (invariant). 
Q2: Arnav's total incoming = 0 + 60 = 60. 
Q3: Bhavna→Arnav is 10 or 20 (exact value-set over S). 
Q4: exactly the 4 loop cells cannot be determined.
